subject: RFP Bakeoff: Matching Credit & Measurement Plan
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFP bakeoff — proposed matched-credit approach

Team,

Per Healthly's RFP timeline, they asked us to surface a clear matched-credit proposal for the bakeoff cohort (two-week benchmark). I sketched an ops-friendly approach below — want alignment before I send to Evan / procurement: 

- Offer: up to $35k in matched credits, paid as consumption credits redeemable in hosted Redwood (no cash).
- Eligibility: limited to their 3 pilot teams; credits expire after 90 days.
- Measurement: tied to two success metrics we asked for — latency p50/p95 and model throughput on their representative workload.
- Governance: require a short MSA addendum + security attestation (SOC2 snapshot).

Attachments: I exported a brief draft: redwood_matched_credit_agreement_v1.pdf and a metrics workbook.

Open questions:
1) Is 90-day expiry OK with finance/legal?
2) How strict should the measurement gating be before credits are unlocked? (full unlock vs staged release)
3) Any reason to route through escrow/escrow-like holdback?

Marissa — can you confirm operational steps (wiring vs credit attachment) and Priyom can you weigh in on commercial sizing?

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales — West
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP bakeoff — proposed matched-credit approach

Tessa — quick notes:

- 90 days is fine operationally but finance prefers a staged unlock: 50% at kickoff, 50% release after benchmark acceptance. That reduces risk if the trial is abandoned.
- We should deliver credits as account-level promo codes tied to the account ID (Healthly) rather than True "wiring" — this avoids cash movement and keeps it simple for accounting.
- Attachments look good; I'll add a short ops checklist: how to redeem, entitlement names, and the internal ledger entry.

I'll patch the pdf with the staged unlock language and send back by EOD. Priyom, does the $35k cover what you expected?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Field Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@healthly.com>, Amy Chen <amy.chen@healthly.com>, procurement@healthly.com
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP bakeoff — proposed matched-credit approach

Evan / Amy — looping you in with our recommended structure so procurement has the mechanics early. Highlights for Healthly: 

- Program: Redwood will provide up to $35,000 in hosting credits for the bakeoff.
- Delivery: 50% of credits applied at project kickoff; remaining 50% applied after mutually-agreed acceptance of benchmark results.
- Compliance: We need a signed short addendum (attached) and a SOC2 attestation snapshot (we can provide).
- Measurement: we propose the attached workbook for acceptance criteria; we can workshop the gating in a 30-min call.

Evan — is the staged release acceptable? If you prefer a single application at kickoff for procurement reasons, let us know and we can rework finance approval (may need a small security deposit).

Priyom Das
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: benchmark-success-metrics.xlsx, redwood_matched_credit_agreement_v1.pdf

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@healthly.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amy Chen <amy.chen@healthly.com>, procurement@healthly.com
Date: Wed, 20 Jan 2027 15:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP bakeoff — proposed matched-credit approach

Thanks — this looks straightforward and much appreciated. A couple of quick clarifications from our side before we sign: 

1) Acceptance gating: we prefer the staged approach you suggested (50/50) but would like the second release after the post-run acceptance call (not automatic) — we want a short signoff list.
2) SOC2 snapshot: please send the latest report and a contact for security questions.
3) On expiry: 90 days is acceptable as long as there is a one-time 30-day extension we can request if there are scheduling delays (no extra credits).

If you can send the addendum with the staged-release language and the SOC2 snapshot we can get legal/procurement to review and aim for a DocuSign turnaround of 3–4 business days.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call Thursday to walk the metrics workbook.

Best,
Evan Brooks
VP Product
Healthly
Phone: +1 415 555 0123
